action.name: Set Battery Health Optimizer from 80 to 70 percent

validation.applyResult: Confirmed captured 07/12 C6 setter and successful typed applies
validation.readbackResult: Confirmed 07/92 C6 at 70 percent and D0 at 80 percent
validation.restorationResult: Restored the saved 80-percent charge limit after every validation
validation.restorationReadbackResult: Confirmed Limit80 by typed firmware readback and visible Synapse state

sanitizedEvidence.summary: The only action-specific charge-limit setter was 07/12 with argument C6 at 28.225041 seconds.
The 30-second idle baseline stopped gracefully and contained no operator charge-limit change.
Three 07/92 00 reads returned C6 at 70 percent and three returned D0 at 80 percent.
80-to-70-to-80 and 80-to-75-to-80 each applied, read back, and restored in both quiet-controller and Synapse-running lighting-off windows.
Three exact production-factory probes exposed only limit 70, opened successfully, and returned confirmed protection enabled at 80 percent.
Active Spectrum traffic produced an unrelated 03/0B response and TransactionMismatch; ten reads succeeded after the operator switched lighting off while Synapse remained running.

productionAdmission.identityScope: RZ09-0528, BIOS 2.02, USB 1532:02C6, HID usage 0001:0002, 91-byte feature reports

limitations: At this charge-limit checkpoint, only the captured 70-percent setter was admitted; later exact-device evidence separately admits temporary full charge.
The 75-percent setter was reversibly validated but was not independently captured, so it is not production-admitted.
Active Synapse Spectrum traffic can race the shared feature response; OpenBlade rejects unrelated acknowledgements.
Keyboard lighting remains off at the operator's request.
Two failed USBPcap query attempts produced no PCAP and are preserved privately as failures, not evidence.
Raw PCAPs and unique device identifiers remain private and uncommitted.
notes: Final charge limit was restored to 80 percent and temporary full charge remained unchecked.
